player.name: Wren Ashdown
player.concept: a quick-witted half-elf ranger with a longbow, a dry sense of humour and a soft spot for underdogs

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Wendell Prout turns slowly above the shut loft door, a pigeon hunched on the hoist beam beside him. Below, a scrawny boy in enormous black boots lobs gutter stones at the body. “Spin, you dead ink-pot! Cob’s got better aim than the hangman!” On the wall, a sharp-faced girl swears at him in Common, then spits a dockside curse after a passing pigeon.

A woman in a rain cape steps away from the gate, notebook in hand. “Sergeant Agnes Kell, investigator. The Captain calls it suicide. I haven’t written that down.” Her eyes flick to your hands, then back to your face. “Where would you like to start?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I study the slowly turning body for a long moment, then turn to Kell. "Start? At the top, Sergeant. That is where he finished." I raise a hand toward the boy without looking at him. "You there, with the boots. Stop that at once. Every stone you throw alters the rate at which he turns, and the rate at which he turns is evidence." I squint up at the body and begin counting under my breath. "How many times has he gone round since you got here, lad? Be precise. A man is hanging on your answer."

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Cob stops mid-throw, stone clenched in his fist. “Cob’s not your lad, and he ain’t counting for you.” He glances at Moll, who gives him a sharp look.

Kell’s mouth twitches. “A precise answer would be useful. But the boy’s got no clock.” She taps her pencil once against her notebook. “And the body’s turning because the wind’s at it, investigator—not because he’s keeping count.”

Moll kicks her heels against the wall. “He jumped, if you’re collecting answers. Midnight. Wailing about his debts. I saw the whole thing.”

Cob makes a rude noise and hefts the stone again, though he doesn’t throw it. The body turns another slow fraction above you.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I turn to the girl on the wall with grave courtesy and take out a stub of pencil. "A witness. Splendid. You say he jumped. Up, or down?" I wait, pencil poised. "Because if he jumped down, he jumped from somewhere, and the only somewhere up there is the loft door. Which is shut." I point at it. "Now. A man who jumps out of a door must first open it. And a man who has just been hanged is in no position to close it behind him. So either the door shut itself out of tact, or somebody else was up there." I make a careful note. "Also, you said wailing. Proper wailing, or just mentioning his debts loudly? It matters." I glance at the pigeon on the hoist beam. "Do not go anywhere, you. You are next."

transcript.text: Insight check to see through Moll's story about the jump: 11 + 3 = 14 vs DC 13: success

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Moll’s smile falters at your questions. Her eyes flick to the shut loft door, then to Cob. “Wasn’t there,” she mutters. “Couldn’t’ve seen it. It rained all night.”

Kell’s pencil pauses. Moll’s fist closes tighter.

“Fine,” Moll spits. “A gentleman paid me a silver crown at first light to say I saw him jump. There. Happy?” She opens her fist just enough to show the wheat-ear stamped on the coin, then hides it again. “He had a fine coat. A silver-topped cane.”

Kell writes carefully. “A paid lie. Noted.” She looks from the coin to the hanging clerk. “Who was he, and what did he want buried with Prout?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I nod gravely to Moll. "Thank you. A paid lie is still evidence. It tells us someone thought a lie was worth a crown." Then I walk beneath the hoist beam, clear my throat, and address the pigeon with full formality. "Sergeant, please record this. Witness statement, the pigeon on the hoist beam." I look up at it. "You were present on that beam last night, or at least you are present now, which in the absence of a better witness I shall treat as the same thing. Did you see a gentleman with a fine coat and a silver-topped cane? Coo once for yes, twice for no." I wait, perfectly serious, pencil ready.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The pigeon blinks, gives one dry coo, and lifts off the beam in a burst of grey wings. It circles the yard once and settles on the granary roof, having declined to testify.

Kell watches it go. “Noted. An uncooperative witness.” She turns a page in her notebook. “We have a paid lie, a shut loft door, and a body hung where it couldn’t hang itself. Now we need the man with the cane—and a reason.”

Moll drops from the wall and catches Cob by the sleeve. He jerks away, one oversized boot scraping the cobbles. “Leave off,” he snaps, but his eyes dart toward the water butt. What do you do?
